_meta.purpose: Declarative registry of count assertions that HAVE a definite backing data source, so the weekly janitor can verify each asserted number still matches computed reality. See wiki/architecture/fact_inventory.md Family 2 and recommendation R5.
_meta.scope_rule: ONLY counts with a real ground truth belong here. Living counts with no authoritative source -- e.g. the sociogram node total, which fact_inventory records as SIX conflicting asserted values with nothing to reconcile against -- must be REMOVED from prose per R4, NOT asserted-and-checked. Do not add them here; adding a count with no stable backing would make the detector itself a source of noise.
_meta.kinds: source.kind 'json_len' = length of the backing JSON: a top-level list, or the list under source.array_key when the top level is an object.
_meta.assertion_rule: Each assertion.pattern MUST capture the number in group 1 and be specific enough that it matches ONLY the count in question. Prefer a distinctive adjacent word (e.g. 'curated', 'communities articulated') over a bare 'N communities', which would collide with unrelated numbers. Commas in the captured number are stripped before comparison.

invariants.reason: The curated community set is exactly the array in curated_communities.json (155, mirrored by community_graph.json). Prose naming a different number (156 today) has drifted -- reconcile the prose to the data, or add the missing community, but the two must agree.
